chunks: From him, from Hammad, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about the salat (prayer) in the month of Ramadan. He said: Thirteen rak'ahs, including al-Witr, and two rak'ahs before Salat al-Fajr. Thus was the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم praying; and if there had been any additional merit, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم would have acted upon it and would have had more right to it.

key_terms.الْوِتْرُ: the Witr prayer included within the total
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم whose practice is cited
key_terms.رَكْعَتَانِ: the two rak'ahs before Salat al-Fajr
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan in which this devotional salat is discussed
key_terms.صَلَاةِ الْفَجْرِ: the dawn prayer before which two rak'ahs are performed

ai.seo_question: How many rak'ahs of salat (prayer) are recommended in Ramadan according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the recommended night salat (prayer) in the month of Ramadan, specifying thirteen rak'ahs including al-Witr and two rak'ahs before Salat al-Fajr. It grounds the ruling in the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, indicating that no superior additional practice was left unperformed by him.
